definition: Test-time compute allocation means deciding, per query, how much inference-time compute or reasoning effort to spend. The RTL-optimization source (ARES) raises an LLM agent's per-call reasoning effort only after progress on a task stalls, reporting normalized dollar cost alongside a power-area-delay figure of merit; 'Strategic Scaling of Test-Time Compute' instead formulates the allocation across queries as a bandit-learning problem, so harder queries receive more compute and easier ones less.

evidence.note: Formulates test-time compute allocation across queries as a bandit learning problem so that harder queries get more compute and easier ones get less.
evidence.title: Strategic Scaling of Test-Time Compute: A Bandit Learning Approach
